unit.why: A single narrative: a woman asks the Maggid for a son, and he tells how his mother obtained his birth from the Besht by giving her garment, then refuses to repeat the remedy.

stories.start_quote: עו״ש שבאה אשה אחת אל המגיד
stories.end_quote: אבל אתה שמעת המעשה מאמי ז״ל
stories.summary_en: A woman asks the Maggid for a son. He tells how his own poor mother gave the Besht her only garment (katinke), wandering in poverty to Medzhybizh to deliver it, and was promised a son to be named Israel. When the woman offers her garment too, he says his mother acted on her own initiative, while she only heard the story.

quotes: ואמר לה שיהא לה ב״ז ותקרא אותו ישראל כשמי
tags.why: The Besht's blessing brings about the birth of a son to the Maggid's mother.
The core narrative is how the Maggid's own birth came about through the Besht.

quotes: אמי ג״כ היתה צריכה לב״ז והלכה להבעש״ט
tags.why: The Maggid's mother is a central character.

quotes: ולקחה את הקאטינקא והלכה מעיר לעיר
tags.why: The mother acts on her own and travels to bring the garment.

quotes: שבאה אשה אחת אל המגיד זצ״ל וביקשה
tags.why: The petitioning woman in the frame story.
The mother journeys to the Besht in Medzhybizh.

quotes: ובתוך כך נסע הבעש״ט לעירו למעזיבוזש
tags.why: The Besht's departure forces her to travel after him.

quotes: ואמר לה מה אתה נותן לי
tags.why: A payment, the garment, is demanded by the tsaddik in exchange for the blessing.
The garment is central to the story and carries religious significance.

quotes: אני ג״כ אביא לכם המלבוש שלי
tags.why: The Maggid receives a petitioner and turns down her proposed remedy.

quotes: אבל אתה שמעת המעשה מאמי ז״ל
tags.why: The Maggid tells the story, and the fact that it was retold matters to the outcome.

quotes: אמי לא היתה יודעת מהקאטינקא רק מעצמה עשתה זאת
tags.why: He explains why the remedy cannot be repeated.

quotes: שהיא אשה עניה ואין לה כלום
tags.why: The mother's poverty and hardship are depicted, though not embraced as a virtue.
She gives everything she has, which is borderline as charity.

quotes: ואמר לה הבעש״ט שתביא אליו את הקאעינקע ואז יהא לה בן זכר
tags.why: The story turns on the tsaddik's power to grant offspring.
The Besht predicts the birth of a son and his name.
The birth is implied as the outcome rather than narrated.

missing_concepts: spontaneity/naivety vs. imitation of a known remedy (self-initiated sacrifice cannot be replicated)
